title: Tenant-Scoped Role Templates and Quick-Assign Flow for Delegated Admins
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem:
Customer feedback and internal audits show that tenant admins need a faster way to assign curated role templates to teams while preserving auditability and justification for high-risk permissions. Current flows require creating or editing granular role bindings per user, which is slow and error-prone for operators managing dozens of projects.

Goals:
- Design a compact "quick-assign" UX for tenant-scoped role templates that lets delegated admins apply a template to users, groups, or service principals in 2–3 interactions.
- Surface a preview of effective permissions and highlight any high-risk scopes (data export, model-pinning, network config) before confirm.
- Capture an optional (and audited) assignment rationale for compliance teams.
- Integrate with existing audit logs so every template application is traceable with before/after snapshots.

Constraints & non-goals:
- This ticket focuses on the Console UX; backend APIs and RBAC enforcement changes are in ENG-5124. We must design within current API responses but allow for small schema additions (assignment_reason, template_version). Not building nested role inheritance in this phase.

Primary users:
- Tenant admins and delegated security leads assigning roles at scale
- Platform engineers who will review permission changes during audits
- Compliance officers who need justification and trace links

Success metrics (linked to PM):
- Reduce median time-to-assign for a role template from 6 minutes to under 90 seconds for common flows
- 90% of template assignments include a non-empty rationale when the template contains high-risk permissions
- No critical accessibility regressions (WCAG AA)
acceptance_criteria: Design includes a 1-panel quick-assign flow: select template -> choose targets (users/groups/service principals) -> preview -> confirm
Permission preview shows aggregated effective permissions with clear high-risk flags and a link to related audit policy docs
Optional assignment rationale captured and stored as part of audit metadata (UI mock shows field and character limits)
Edge states addressed: empty group, conflicting existing bindings, failed assignment API error mapping
Design annotated for developers with API fields required (template_id, template_version, assignee_ids, assignment_reason)
Accessibility checklist completed and keyboard-first flows validated in mocks
design_notes: Use compact tokenized chips for selected users/groups; support paste-to-multi-add from comma/newline list
Preview uses a split list: left = granted actions (grouped by resource), right = risk indicators with inline help popovers
If template includes 'admin-level' flags, show a required justification text area and append a checkbox: 'record for audit' (default on)
Include an 'apply as: template version' dropdown to make rollbacks/traceability easier
Keep the flow as a transient modal with deep link to 'assignment history' for the affected users
Design small-screen variant: stack sections, collapse permission preview behind a 'show details' toggle
decisions: Prefer tokenized multi-select for assignees vs. table-based bulk upload to reduce cognitive load
Require explicit assignment reason only when any permission in template is marked high-risk; otherwise keep it optional
Audit metadata will capture template_version to support retroactive rollback and investigation
Conflict resolution UI will surface existing bindings and offer 'override' or 'create complementary binding' options (final behavior deferred to ENG)
Do not introduce nested role inheritance in this iteration to keep scope manageable
open_questions: How should we surface historical template changes in the assignment preview if template_version differs from previously applied versions? (ENG input required)
Should group membership expansion be performed client-side (to estimate impacted users) or server-side? trade-offs: latency vs. accuracy
What is the maximum number of assignees we should allow in one quick-assign operation before recommending a CSV import?
Do compliance teams need a separate 'long form' justification stored in a dedicated retention bucket (legal/PM input)
How to represent overlapping permissions from multiple templates in the preview without overwhelming users?
